live_intro: A machine-learning model reproduces SFINCS in about a second. It is a preview, not a simulation, and it is less reliable outside its training range.
live_result: Surrogate model, not SFINCS: {km} km² deeper than 0.5 m, maximum depth {max} m.
live_warn: Outside the training range (rain 33 to 166 mm, lake 769.9 to 773.0 m): extrapolation, not reliable.
d_caveat: This map is a non-commercial research demo. Depths are modelled, not observed, and the model is not calibrated on any real flood. It floods too much. For official alerts, see IGEBU and Burundi's civil protection. Do not use these numbers to decide on an evacuation.
d_states: Observed: surveyed or mapped by others (OpenStreetMap). Modelled: computed by a model (SFINCS, canopy height estimated by machine learning, model-corrected terrain). Assumed: the result of a rule I applied (population allocation, neighbourhoods, priority rank).
d_what: Three storms simulated with SFINCS at 20 m: maximum water depth, affected buildings and an estimate of the people involved. Lake level: 772.50 m (scenarios 1 and 2) and 772.95 m (scenario 3).
d_ev_cop: Against the Copernicus EMSN191 model (scenario 4, the same conditions as scenario 3): CSI {csi}, hit rate {hit}, false-alarm ratio {far}. It finds almost everything Copernicus floods, but floods about 40% more area ({model} km² against {ref} km²).
d_ev_gfm: Against Sentinel-1 in 2024: the satellite saw only {obs} km² of flooding against {model} km² modelled. 2024 was mostly a lake rise, so this test does not measure storm-flood quality.
d_ev_sur: The surrogate model reproduces SFINCS with a CSI of {s0} to {s1} on unseen storms and {c0} to {c1} on an unseen catchment.
d_s1_note: Scenario 1 predates a model fix (curve numbers); the measured effect on the other scenarios is under 1%.
d_datum: The lake level is 772.50 m (EGM2008, the 2024 peak). A press figure of about 777 m is a local gauge reading: do not mix the two.
d_lake: Lake Tanganyika is excluded from areas and colours: the model shows about 2.5 m of water there, which is open water, not flooding.
d_people: People come from WorldPop 2020, shared among buildings by floor area. The estimate can be wrong in informal areas. Counts are rounded and shown per area, never per building. Neighbourhoods are cells around 77 points, not official boundaries.
d_veg: Canopy comes from the Meta and WRI canopy height map (estimated from satellite images, 1 m), shifted 6 m north and 4 m east to match building footprints, then aggregated to 5 m. Trees are the {n} crowns detected on that map. No species are given.

d_lic_terrain: Terrain: FABDEM, University of Bristol / Fathom, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. It limits this demo to non-commercial use.
d_lic_buildings: Buildings: Google Open Buildings (CC BY 4.0) and © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL).
d_lic_veg: Canopy and trees: Meta and WRI, High Resolution Canopy Height (CC BY 4.0).
d_lic_pop: Population: WorldPop, University of Southampton (CC BY 4.0), aggregated only.
d_lic_flood: Modelled floods: Bujumbura Flood Twin (CC BY 4.0).
d_lic_rivers: Rivers: hydro-enforced DEM drainage, after HydroRIVERS (Lehner and Grill, 2013) and OpenStreetMap.
